column1: # P4-209 (#632) criterion 3 — enforcement inventory for infallible allocations
# `vec![…]`, `Vec::with_capacity(…)` and `.to_vec()` abort the process when the
# allocator refuses: there is no Result to return. For a size that comes out of
# a JPEG stream that turns a hostile — or merely large — file into an
# uncatchable denial of service, so every such size goes through
# `JpegError::AllocationFailed`. This file pins the infallible allocations
# that REMAIN, each with the reason its size is bounded by something other than
# `tests/decode_alloc_gate.rs` fails if this file and the sources disagree, so a
# new infallible allocation under src/decode/ cannot land without a human either
# converting it or classifying it here.
# SCOPE: non-test library code under src/decode/ — `//` comment lines,
# `#[cfg(test)] mod … { … }` blocks and `*_tests.rs` files are skipped. The
# three patterns are textual, so an input-sized allocation spelled another way
# (`.clone()` of a Vec, `.collect()` into a Vec, `String::from`) is NOT seen.
#   fixed-size                   a literal or constant length, independent of the input
#   component-count              a per-component list; SOF/SOS parsing caps the count at MAX_COMPONENTS (4)
#   row-scratch                  one row of samples, capped by the SOF's 16-bit width (x2 max scale, x4 bpp: <= 512 KiB)
#   infallible-public-signature  inside a public fn whose signature cannot carry an error; size is a buffer the caller already holds
